declarations.name: Blocked
declarations.description: Tests the KERNEL-BLOCKED guard: attributes whose DOM name elm/virtual-dom rewrites or ignores get no setter on any surface, while a legitimate sibling attribute on the same element still does.

attributes.name: formaction
attributes.description: BLOCKED. `_VirtualDom_RE_on_formAction` is /^(on|formAction$)/i, and the `i` flag makes `^formAction$` match HTML's lowercase `formaction`, so `_VirtualDom_noOnOrFormAction` rewrites the key to `data-formaction`. The property path is closed too, so there is no working path from Elm.

attributes.name: onbeforetoggle
attributes.description: BLOCKED by the `^on` half of the same regex — the future-proofing case. No `on*` content attribute is in a real manifest today; a manifest refresh that adds one must not ship a dead setter.

attributes.name: once
attributes.description: BLOCKED, and deliberately an INNOCENT name: `^on` is a prefix with no word boundary, so the kernel regex matches `once` too and renders it as `data-once`. The kernel over-reaches; the honest response is to report it, not to emit a setter that lies.

attributes.name: is
attributes.description: BLOCKED. A customized built-in needs `document.createElement(tag, { is })` at creation time, and `_VirtualDom_render` calls `createElement(vNode.__tag)` with no options argument. Declared per-component here (hostile has no `_globals` roster) so the guard is proven on the COMPONENT path; elm-typed-html proves it on the globals path.

attributes.name: innerhtml
attributes.description: BLOCKED only in the PROPERTY form, which config `attrForm` selects here: `_VirtualDom_noInnerHtmlOrFormAction` rewrites the property key `innerHTML` to `data-innerHTML`. Proves the guard reads the form, since the same spec as a content attribute would not be blocked.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: NOT blocked — the control. Proves the guard is selective rather than emptying the element's surface, and that a blocked sibling does not take the whole `Attrs` row with it.
